output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mainly a Quillbook connector problem, not a pricing problem. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices: 58,300 across 1,212 accounts. Of those accounts, 34% had cancelled by July, against 8% of Quillbook accounts with no recorded failure. Quillbook-connected accounts, repriced or price-locked, jumped from about 2% to about 6% monthly churn. Accounts with no connector, repriced and at every seat size, stayed at about 1.9%. The seat-size pattern in the finance analysis arises because Quillbook accounts have more seats. The price signals in the exit surveys and renewal calls are probably complaints about value, not the cause. I am fairly confident in this. The exact Tallymarsh effect is unproven, and its error log has not been reviewed.

Next steps: 1) Make the Quillbook fix to the new interface (3–4 weeks) the top engineering priority, and contact every Quillbook account, including those that cancelled, to correct their invoices. 2) Do not roll back the price, which would cost about $220k a month. 3) Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on. 4) Review the Tallymarsh log before committing a team to a rebuild. 5) Fix the monitoring so it counts WARN events.
